title: Weekly eng brief: serving runtime pulse & synthesis — Aug 02 2026
content:
TL;DR: Focus this week on stabilizing the producer-side batching regressions spotted after the A/B rollout (small latency tail increase for 2% of requests), finish the canary for v2.3.1 quantized kernels, and land the KV-cache eviction telemetry so SRE can tune the autoscaler. Ops had a short P2 (30m) Thursday — cause traced to a rare memory spike when a specific long-chat workload triggered blockwise attention path; mitigation: temporary soft-limit + rollout pause for affected customers.

Agenda for this note:
- Wins / completed work
- Incident recap + follow-ups
- Performance metrics (high level)
- Ongoing rollouts and gating decisions
- Blockers and asks (what we need from other teams)
- Action items and owners
- Open questions + discussion prompts for the org meeting

Wins (shoutouts)
- Diego: landed the kernel selection feature that reduces CPU overhead for short sequences in mixed-batch scenarios (internal PR #2184). Early internal perf tests show 6–9% CPU cost reduction on p4d for tiny-req workloads.
- Priya & Lena: finished instrumentation for prefix/KV cache eviction events — logs now include eviction_reason, sequence_len, and upstream-request-id. This is already giving SRE better signal.
- Cluster team: autoscaler change to prefer more small instances reduced cold-start rate by ~12% on Tuesday (data from metrics pipeline).
- Solutions Eng: two customers on Dedicated saw 18% cost reduction after enabling the new quantized Llama-variant and batching profile.

Incident recap (P2, Thu 2026-07-30 14:12–14:42 UTC)
- Symptom: a subset (~2.1%) of production inference calls hit 95th/99th latency degradation (+80–150ms) and higher memory allocations; request patterns were long-conversation streams with intermittent short replies.
- Root cause timeline: Repro showed pathological switch to blockwise-attention kernel when prefix length + user-turn length combined crossed a heuristic boundary. That kernel path currently allocates a transient buffer that in rare interleaved requests caused temporary spike.
- Mitigation applied: rolled back new heuristic (reverted feature flag for heuristic 3) and enabled a soft memory cap per worker. Canary paused for customers with >50 concurrent streams.
- Postmortem next steps: add unit tests for the combined-length boundary (Samir), make transient buffer allocation poolable (engineering infra), and add an alert that triggers at 60% of worker memory (SRE).

Performance snapshot (last 7 days) — high level
- p50/p90/p99 tokens-per-second (aggregate serving-rx): 420 / 260 / 115
- Avg token cost: down 3.7% week-over-week due to caching tweaks
- CPU tail behavior: small bump observed on Tuesday that correlates with the kernel selection rollout; after rollback latencies normalizing, but watch p95 over next 48h.
- KV-cache hit rate (hosted models): 72% global; targeted customers in B2B cohort have 78–82% after tuning.

Ongoing rollouts and gating decisions
- Quantized kernels v2.3.1 (canary): progress at 55% traffic for internal test tenants. Tests show 2–3x throughput improvement for 8-bit paths on A100 but there are small semantic diffs we are evaluating. Gate: must have no regression in hallucination eval on the acceptance prompt set and end-to-end latency p99 <= baseline + 30ms. Decision expected by Fri EOD.
- Routing policy change: smart-routing by latency tier (experiment): running for 4 days; initial results: 9% cost saving, 1.4% increase in cross-region requests; need privacy review for cross-region fallback (security).
- Canary pause: model-pinning rollout for enterprise tier paused until KV eviction telemetry rolled out to all Dedicated clusters.

Blockers / asks
- Observability team: need a short retention increase (+7 days) for eviction logs for one customer bucket to complete regression analysis (Priya).
- Security: quick review of the smart-routing cross-region data flow — legal flagged potential EUDTP compliance question (Samir will route the summary).
- Product: decision on rollback policy for quantized-kernels (should compute roll-forward vs rollback threshold for hallucination delta). We need product sign-off by Friday.

Action items (owner — ETA)
1) Add unit tests for combined-length boundary + fuzz cases (Samir) — ETA 2026-08-06
2) Implement pooled transient buffers to avoid spikes (Diego + infra) — ETA 2026-08-13
3) Finish KV-cache eviction telemetry backfill and increase retention for selected peer buckets (Priya) — ETA 2026-08-05
4) SRE to add memory usage alert at 60% for worker processes + run chaos job for mem pressure (Lena) — ETA 2026-08-07
5) Data science: run hallucination eval sweep on v2.3.1 canary with acceptance prompts and report confidence intervals (R&D) — ETA 2026-08-04
6) Product + Legal: finalize cross-region fallback policy and put decision in Confluence (Product Manager: Arjun Patel) — ETA 2026-08-06

Meeting notes / topics to bring to org-wide update (all-hands)
- Brief on incident: quick summary + what we changed (2 slides). Keep it high-level: heuristic rollback, mitigation, ongoing fixes.
- Show metrics slide: KV-cache hit-rate improvement and p50/p95 improvement after autoscaler tweak.
- Ask-for-help slide: we need observability retention and legal's quick review of routing policy.
- Roadmap highlight: kernel selection landing + quantized-kernels decision timeline.

Unresolved questions / prompts
- Is our current baseline for hallucination delta (used as gating) too strict for 8-bit kernels? Product has suggested raising the tolerance for ambiguous prompts — what are the trade-offs?
- For Dedicated customers with strict ROI requirements, should we expose an opt-in toggle for kernel aggressiveness? (perf vs determinism).

Notes-to-self + working thoughts (informal)
- Consider adding a microbenchmark harness that replays mixed-length conversations with background noise to exercise the heuristic boundary continuously in CI.
- We should tag the canary clients where we saw the blockwise path frequently so we can repro faster.
- If pooled buffer approach looks heavy, fallback plan: strengthen heuristic to avoid boundary oscillation and add randomized jitter to kernel choice.

Quick links referenced in this note:
- internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2184
- Linear ticket: https://linear.app/REDW/issue/R-482-model-rollback
- Confluence draft: confluence://runtime/kv-cache-performance

Shoutouts again: Diego for kernel selection work, Priya for telemetry push, Lena for autoscaler follow-through. Thanks team — please update your progress in the action-item thread (Slack #eng-serving-runtime) and ping me if you want to demo the kernel selection perf graphs in the next all-hands.

End of note.
